thread:
Alex (AcmeCorp): Hey team — we hit our monthly credits at ~23:58 PT and expected the monthly refill at 00:00 local, but at 00:05 we were still getting 429 quota_exceeded from the API. Console shows the credits were added at 00:00, but API calls from prod still failing. This caused a visible outage for users. Can someone explain why the UI shows credits but the API still enforces limit? Urgent — rolling back feature now.

Emma (Support): Sorry about the outage, Alex — we'll take a look. Quick questions: what's your org id or account email? Do you use Hosted API or Dedicated capacity? Any sample request IDs or response headers from the 429s?

Alex (AcmeCorp): Org: org-A12345, email alex@acmecorp.com. We're on Hosted API. Sample response headers from one of the failed requests: 

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rw-quota-reset: 2026-03-01T00:00:00Z
x-rw-remaining-tokens: 0
x-rw-request-id: r-0f3c9a2b
content-type: application/json
```

Console screenshot (we attached) shows balance: 1,000,000 tokens added at 00:00. But every request kept getting 429 until ~00:07.

Kai (Support): Thanks — that's helpful. Two likely causes: 1) metering vs enforcement gap: our billing/metering pipeline can update UI quickly when monthly allocation hits, but the enforcement token-bucket used at the edge gateway caches token counts for stability for a short TTL. If you were in a high burst at the moment of reset, the cached bucket can still reflect pre-reset depleted state until the gateway refreshes. 2) If you sent a huge concurrent burst right at reset, the rate limiter could throttle while the new tokens get gradually added to the in-memory bucket (we do gradual refill to avoid massive instantaneous bursts).

Emma (Support): Pragmatically, we can do two things right now: 1) apply a temporary override/unblock on org-A12345 for ~10 minutes so your traffic can catch up, and 2) escalate to infra to check edge cache refresh behavior for your org around that reset time. Which do you want us to do now?

Alex (AcmeCorp): Please apply the temporary unblock — we need traffic restored. Also we need steps to reproduce so we can avoid this in the future (or schedule resets).

Lina (Billing): Adding context from billing: monthly allocations are created at 00:00 UTC for most accounts by default. The billing ledger writes the new allocation immediately, and the Console reads from that ledger, so UI shows tokens at 00:00 UTC. Enforcement, however, is done by the serving gateway which relies on a cached token-bucket per org; that cache poll interval is short but not instantaneous. For customers who need deterministic local-midnight reset, we offer timezone-anchored resets as an enterprise option (we can check if your account has that).

Emma (Support): For reproducibility, Kai — can you suggest a minimal test we can run that simulates this? If we capture headers and timestamps we can prove the TTL lag.

Kai (Support): Yep — here's a simple repro script you can run from any host (run against prod with your API key in a non-prod org if you want to test). It floods until quota=0, then continues sending at reset and records headers.

```
#!/bin/bash
API_KEY="${API_KEY}"
URL="https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate"
# loop until we see 429
while true; do
  resp=$(curl -s -D - -o /dev/null -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" -X POST $URL -d '{"input":"hello"}')
  echo "$resp" | egrep "x-rw-remaining-tokens|x-rw-quota-reset|x-rw-request-id"
  if echo "$resp" | grep -q "429"; then break; fi
done
# sleep until just before expected reset, then continue and log headers
# watch the headers around reset and compare console timestamp vs headers
```

Kai (Support): Key things to watch for: the `x-rw-quota-reset` value (UTC timestamp), `x-rw-remaining-tokens`, and any `x-rw-cache-ttl` header we sometimes inject for debugging. If remaining stays zero after the ledger shows allocation, it indicates the gateway cache hasn't picked up the new ledger entry.

Alex (AcmeCorp): Ok we'll run that during next window in a staging org. For now, thanks for the unblock. Any SLA note we should put in our postmortem? Need to include root cause.

Emma (Support): We'll open an internal ticket and a postmortem entry. Initial classification: enforcement cache TTL + burst-edge behavior around reset. Action items: 
- Temporary unblock applied (SUP-12345).
- Infra to review gateway cache poll interval and consider immediate refresh on monthly ledger event.
- Docs update: clarify UI shows ledger allocation vs enforcement timing; add guidance on scheduling bulk jobs around resets.

infra-bot: Deploy job queued: infra/edge-cache-refresh-investigation, assigned to @kai, ETA 48h.

Lina (Billing): Also noting: if your org needs deterministic local-midnight resets (PST), we can evaluate migrating your billing timezone and enable timezone-anchored resets; that requires a billing config change and will be scheduled for next cycle. I'll open a billing ticket and cc you.

Alex (AcmeCorp): All good. Please include the exact timestamps (00:00 UTC vs our local midnight) in the postmortem so we can present to our ops team. Appreciate the fast response.

Emma (Support): Will do — closing this Slack thread once infra confirms investigation kickoff. We'll post SUP-12345 updates here. Thanks for the detailed headers, Alex — that made triage quick. :thumbsup:
